newsitem.title: UK: Call for UK Tory rank and file voice over leader.
newsitem.headline: Call for UK Tory rank and file voice over leader.

text.p: Brian Mawhinney, the chairman of Britain's opposition Conservative party, intervened in the debate on how the party's new leader should be elected on Tuesday, putting forward a plan to give ordinary party members limited influence.
Mawhinney said he did not want to see the election to replace John Major decided simply by the 164 MPs, who survived the party's hammering at the polls on May 1.
The parliamentary party now does not include a single member representing a Scottish or Welsh constituency, and there are few sitting for seats in major cities in England.
In an open letter, Mawhinney said he proposed, at least for the forthcoming election, an electoral college in which the MPs would have 85 percent of the votes and constituency chairmen 15 percent.

"This would mean that all members of the Party would be able to contribute to the electoral process through their own local representative. Constituency chairmen are already bound to ascertain the views of their Association membership," Mawhinney said.
Mawhinney addressed the letter to his fellow MPs, who together constitute the 1922 Committee, which will make arrangements for the leadership contest.
"The new leader needs to have, and be seen to have, the unambiguous support of both the parliamentary and voluntary members of the Party," he said.
Six former Cabinet ministers have declared themselves candidates to replace Major.

Several of them have expressed sympathy with the aim of greater internal democracy in choosing the party leader, although they have in some cases expressed doubts whether it would take too long to set up a new system for the present contest.
